title: Yomyom (brass pellet bells)
summary: The yomyom is a string of small brass pellet bells named for its sound and worn by Igbo dancers on the ankles or waist. Pellet rattles encased in metal are threaded in rows and tied to the body, jingling with the dancer's movement.
howToPlay: Three rows of bells are lit: High for the smallest, Mid, and Low for the biggest.
The row you strike shakes and rings; the bigger the bells, the lower the sound.
A ring closes on the row to strike. Let them ring a little before the next.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The bells are threaded in rows and sound with every movement of the dancer, adding a bright jingle above the drums.
